hints.S33_A1: He did not run from his FEAR OF HEIGHTS - he climbed the wall STEP BY STEP until the fear was beaten. Ask: which verb means to overcome something completely? 'Avoided' and 'ignored' would mean he never faced it at all.
hints.S33_A2: She is standing AT THE EDGE OF THE DIVING BOARD FOR THE FIRST TIME, and her body is showing her nerves. Ask: which verb shows hands shaking with fear? 'Relaxed' would mean she felt perfectly calm.
hints.S33_A3: The coach's words are kind: SHE HAD TRAINED HARD AND WAS READY, and the swimmer is NERVOUS. Ask: which verb means calming someone by giving them confidence? 'Scolded' and 'criticised' would only make her feel worse.
hints.S33_A4: She FAILED THE AUDITION TWICE and still went back A THIRD TIME. Ask: which noun names the quality of carrying on in spite of failure? 'Laziness' and 'cowardice' would have kept her at home.
hints.S33_A5: Nobody dares make a sound: the gymnast is performing HER MOST DIFFICULT ROUTINE and the AUDIENCE is holding its breath. Ask: which adjective describes a silence full of suspense? 'Bored' and 'restless' would mean nobody cared.
hints.S33_B1: The pattern is 'HELP + person + verb', and the person is STUDENTS, a plural. Ask: after 'help students', do we use the plain verb or the one with -s? EVERY YEAR keeps the whole sentence in the present.
hints.S33_B2: AT THE FINALS she DELIVERED A PERFECT PERFORMANCE - both actions are over and done. Ask: which form shows a finished past action? This verb is regular, so no vowel change is needed, just the ordinary ending.
hints.S33_B3: IT STARTED TO RAIN HEAVILY - a sudden event cutting into something already under way. Ask: which choice keeps the students in the middle of the HIGH ROPES COURSE at that past moment? A plain past verb would say the job was over.
hints.S33_B4: NEVER TRIED ROCK CLIMBING BEFORE - the statement is a negative one. Ask: after a negative statement, does the tag stay negative or flip to positive? The tag must repeat the statement's own helping verb, so 'did' is out of place.
hints.S33_B5: The statement is positive and past: the speech WAS DELIVERED BRAVELY. Ask: after a positive statement, does the tag flip to negative, or stay positive? A tag always keeps the tense the statement gives it.
hints.S33_B6: 'A LONG SILENCE' is one thing, not several, and THE RESULTS WERE ANNOUNCED sets the time in the past. Ask: does a singular subject take a present form, or a past one? 'Were' would need a plural subject.
hints.S33_B7: THE GOLD MEDAL did nothing at all - THE YOUNGEST COMPETITOR did it. Ask: which choice puts the subject on the receiving end of a past action? Passive = a form of 'be' + the past participle.
hints.S33_B8: TOLD THE ANXIOUS STUDENT = a reported command, and a negative one: she must stop being HARSH with HERSELF. Ask: which negative word comes first, and which verb form follows it - plain, -ing, or the infinitive?
hints.S33_C1: Nora is asking about a thing - THE WORST THING THAT COULD HAPPEN - not about a person or a time. Ask: which question word asks about things and events? A person word would need somebody to point at.
hints.S33_C2: She wants a reason, and the passage supplies it at once: the fear was ABOUT BEING JUDGED BY OTHERS. Ask: which question word asks for a reason? 'How' would ask about the method instead.
hints.S33_C3: The blank points at people IN THE AUDIENCE she TRUSTED, and she focuses on THEIR FRIENDLY FACES. Ask: which question word asks about a person? 'Which' would force her to choose from a fixed list.
hints.S33_C4: The dash gives the answer away as a place: HER BEDROOM, STANDING IN FRONT OF THE MIRROR. Ask: which question word asks about a location? A time word would need a clock or a date, not a room.
hints.S33_C5: This blank is about a moment in time - the day HER TEACHER FIRST TOLD HER she had a gift. Ask: which question word asks about time? The place word has already been used for her bedroom.
hints.S33_C6: She is thinking about the manner of her OPENING LINE - she wants to deliver it WITH CONFIDENCE. Ask: which question word asks in what way something is done? A thing word would ask which line, not the way she says it.
hints.S33_C7: Count them: OF HER TWO PREPARED ENDINGS - the choice comes from a fixed, limited set. Ask: does the open question word belong here, or the choosing one? Use the choosing word whenever the options are already listed.
hints.S33_C8: The blank stands directly in front of the noun SPEECH, and the sentence ends by naming the owner: IT WAS NORA'S. Ask: which question word asks who something belongs to? A plain person word cannot stand before a noun like this.
hints.S33_D1: The dash defines it: THE FEELING OF WORRY AND NERVOUSNESS before doing something difficult. Ask: which box word names that feeling? The blank follows 'dealing with', so it must be a noun, not a describing word.
hints.S33_D2: He stood AT THE EDGE OF THE POOL FOR SEVERAL MINUTES, UNSURE WHETHER HE COULD DO IT. Ask: which box word means paused because of doubt? 'Stumbled' would mean he tripped, and that is not what held him back.
hints.S33_D3: The clue is in the very same sentence: it DOES NOT MEAN HAVING NO FEAR - it means ACTING DESPITE THE FEAR. Ask: which box word describes a person who acts although afraid? The blank follows 'being', so a noun cannot fit.
hints.S33_D4: Each one is something Marcus OVERCAME IN TRAINING, and each MADE HIM STRONGER AND MORE CONFIDENT. Ask: which box word names a difficulty standing in your way? After 'each', the noun must be singular.
hints.S33_D5: He is STANDING ON THE PODIUM after swimming HIS BEST RACE EVER, and it is THE REWARD for months of hard work. Ask: which box word names a great victory? 'Anxiety' is what he felt at the start, not here.
hints.S33_E1: The underlined word describes HOW the students STEPPED onto the stage - and stepping is an action. Ask: can an adjective describe an action, or does an action need an adverb? Listen for the missing tail on the word.
hints.S33_E2: MANY CHILDS is wrong twice over: this noun never takes a plain -s. Ask: what is the plural of 'child'? It is one of the few English nouns that grows a completely new ending instead.
hints.S33_E3: 'TRY' ends in a consonant plus -y. Ask: what happens to that -y before you add -ed? Compare: cry becomes cried, carry becomes carried, study becomes studied.
hints.S33_E4: THE STUDENTS is plural - the whole group is standing in the wings. Ask: does a plural subject take 'was', or its plural partner? Match the verb to the subject, never to the word standing beside it.
hints.S33_E5: The WARM FEEDBACK came from more than one coach - the whole coaching team. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or only number? Where does the apostrophe belong when the owners are many?
hints.S33_F1: Sentence A sets the condition; sentence B is what follows from it. Ask: after 'If', does the verb stay in the simple present, or take a future helper? Only the second half of the sentence may look forward.
hints.S33_F2: The coach spoke straight to MARCUS and said 'YOU'. Ask: which pronoun takes over when the words are reported to somebody else? And when 'said' becomes 'told', what happens to the word TODAY, and to the tense of the verb?
